newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia govt to tighten foreign tax laws.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia govt to tighten foreign tax laws.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Wednesday the government would tighten taxation arrangements in relation to international companies. Costello said he was aware that a number of Australian institutions were avoiding taxation commitments through loan agreements with foreign companies which had the effect of converting foreign interest income into dividends.
"They do that by attaching sufficient voting rights to eligible finance schemes (EFS) to obtain tax benefits which are afforded to direct equity investments," Costello told parliament.
"EFSs are excluded from the controlled foreign companies and the foreign investment funds measures because they are, in effect, debt and not equity."
He said the government would act to ensure dividends that should be classified as interest income was not granted the tax exemption provided for a direct equity investment in a foreign company.
The government would also withhold tax credits for foreign companies that were found to be involved in such schemes, he said.
"This is a part of a number of measures which the government intends to take to tighten the application of the taxation system, particularly in relation to international measures," Costello said.
Late last year, the government published a discussion paper on possible legislative changes aimed at tightening the taxation system in relation to international arrangements.
Costello said the government was currently receiving public comment on the paper.
